title: GIT-G recovery: `git-recovery` inventories unique state and classifies the recovery path (read-only); `--preserve` adds recovery refs and touches nothing else; git-recovery subskill
objective: Make PRESERVE -> IDENTIFY -> CLASSIFY measured records. `badf_gate.py git-recovery [<path>]` renders the before-state record the recovery contract requires: the git-baseline plus the unique-state inventory (uncommitted changes as a count, stash entries, dangling commits = reflog entries of HEAD unreachable from any ref, unpushed commits per local branch, other worktrees of the same repository), the recovery class (EVIDENCE_ONLY / LOCAL / TOPIC / PROTECTED) and the disposition (RECOVERABLE, or RECOVERY_REQUIRED when unique state must be preserved first), with the least-destructive path as text; unmerged paths are BLOCKED. `--preserve <label> --wp <WP>` creates refs/recovery/<WP>/<label> at HEAD and, for a dirty tree, a -worktree ref at a `git stash create` snapshot (objects written, nothing else moved; an existing label is never overwritten). The tool never resets, cleans, checks out, pushes, deletes a branch/worktree or a ref. The revert pattern for landed work -- including GIT-F's BLOCKED-reconcile path -- is the git-recovery subskill's procedure: a new recovery work package with git revert composed against current main; main is never rewritten.
business_value: The contract stops mutation until unknown state is classified and GIT-O5 requires an inventory and a preservation before any exception, yet nothing produced either; GIT-F's BLOCKED reconcile ended at 'open recovery'; this program's preservation was hand-typed backup branches and its one unclassified residue was met with a hand-run checkout. With the record, a destructive step is safe to CONSIDER and its cost is written down first -- GTGM v0.1 sections 12, 15 and 17 (GIT-G).

out_of_scope: any destructive operation (reset --hard, clean, forced ref moves, branch/worktree deletion, tag rewrites) -- the tool makes them safe to consider, never performs them
executing a revert or opening the recovery work package (the procedure); release-ref recovery -- GIT-H; the remote-workspace mode (#133)
acceptance_criteria: clean detached checkout -> EVIDENCE_ONLY RECOVERABLE with zero unique state; uncommitted + stash -> LOCAL RECOVERY_REQUIRED, counts only, no path or content; a reset-away commit -> inventoried as dangling with the reflog -> recovery-ref path; unpushed topic commits -> TOPIC; HEAD on the default branch -> PROTECTED; other worktrees listed, never the caller's own

--preserve on a dirty tree adds exactly two refs (HEAD + stash-create snapshot whose tree holds the dirty content) and leaves status, index, stash list, reflog and HEAD unchanged; on a clean tree one ref; an existing label is refused; --preserve without --wp is a usage error

refusals BLOCKED outside a repository, on an unborn HEAD and on unmerged paths; the inventory is read-only and deterministic modulo observed_at; each classification, preservation and refusal branch load-bearing (mutation)
